feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 0 (baseline, ±0.024 m, 0.6 kg, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m radius) is the best design at 356.6. It finishes the oval 20/20 at 1.65 s with oscillation 0.15, but its s-bend (0.17) and slalom (0.12) fail at max_error about 0.061 m. Iterations 1 and 2 show that the wider array gives a partial bend gain (s-bend 0.17 to 0.24 and 0.20; slalom 0.12 to 0.19 and 0.12). However, both lost oval finishes (17/20 and 15/20), and the 0.5 kg mass and narrower track were confounded with the spread. Iterations 3 to 5 show that lead and footprint are sharp optima: y=0.07, y=0.03 and an 8 mm footprint each collapsed the oval to 0/20. I kept the iteration-0 controller so that only the spread changes. Interpret the next race as follows. If the oval finishes at 20/20 near 1.65 s and bend progress rises above 0.17 and 0.12, keep ±0.032 m and consider a modest further widening. If the oval drops below 20/20 or oscillation rises above about 0.2, the wide array is not the cure. Then return to ±0.024 m and test the drivetrain alone.
requested_changes: If the oval holds at 20/20 and s-bend or slalom progress rises above 0.17 or 0.12, keep x at ±0.032 m and test x at ±0.040 m at 20 mm pitch, with mass 0.6 kg, since iterations 1 and 2 showed a partial bend gain from spread.

If the oval falls below 20/20 or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 (baseline 0.15), return x to ±0.024 m and test wheel_track 0.11 m alone at 0.6 kg, because the track effect was never isolated from the 0.5 kg mass in iteration 1.
Keep sensor y at 0.05 m, sensor_size at 0.012 m and mass at 0.6 kg for the next test, since iterations 3 to 5 showed the oval collapses when any of these moves alone.
